content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). Steps: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide via coupling (amide formation). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine (step 1 reversed). Then break α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (step 2 reversed). Then break sulfonamide to amine and sulfonyl chloride (step 3 reversed). So we need to find appropriate precursors.

We need templates for each step. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'

This is a retro template: product (amide with alkene) -> reactants: a tert-butyl ester? Actually left side is amide with alkene; right side is t-butyl ester and carboxylic acid? Wait: The right side includes "C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C...]" which is t-butyl ester of the acid, and "O-C(=O)-[CH...]=[C]" which is a carboxylic acid? Actually O-C(=O)-[CH]=[C] is a carboxylic acid with alkene? So this template splits amide into a t-butyl ester of the amide carbonyl and a carboxylic acid containing the alkene? Might be not exactly.

But we can still use it to generate precursors: apply template to target to get two fragments: one is a t-butyl ester of the amide carbonyl (maybe not needed) and the other is the acid part.

But we need three steps: final step is sulfonamide formation: we need sulfonyl chloride and aniline. The target has sulfonamide linking a tolyl amine (para methyl phenyl) to a phenyl sulfone attached to the rest of molecule. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic ring (p-chlorosulfonyl phenyl?). Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be the sulfonyl group attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So precursor: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and p-chlorosulfonyl phenyl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is Ar-SO2Cl. The target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be that phenyl sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph (with the rest of substituent). So we need to generate that.

Thus step 3 (retro) splits target into two: aniline (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride aromatic with the rest (c2ccc(... )cc2) attached to SO2Cl.

We need a template for sulfonamide formation. Let's search for template with functional_groups_broken: primary amines, sulfonyl chloride; formed: sulfonamides. Use search with those groups.
